findings.reason: a node building the test over a fresh-id re-queue tests a stream the refusal path never produces, and can pass its gate while the real path still draws `dropped`; the Why and the fixture must name the same id restored and the release-withdrawal as the row's source.
findings.text: §80's Why asserts "The admission pass re-queues a refused launch under a fresh run id", and its Done-when builds the fixture the same way ("a refused launch of it and its re-queue under a fresh id"), but a refused launch is re-queued under the request's own id: `_record_queued_failure` retains `requeued_run_id or str(snapshot["run_id"])` and a plain refusal leaves `requeued_run_id` empty, since only `LaneHeld`/`LanePaused` carrying a queued record sets it (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:1200-1216`), and `_restore_queued` writes the pointer back with `_write_pointer(str(snapshot["run_id"]), restored)` (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:815`). That same function's docstring names the real source of the `dropped` row — "a request whose release already withdrew it" — so the release of the request's own pointer draws the withdrawal and one run id goes `dropped → queued`, which is what the reported pane shows.

findings.reason: the node locates the records by the run ids the same sentence gives, so the wrong day alone cannot send it to the wrong records.
findings.text: §80 dates the incident "On 2026-10-22 … refused with `PlanReviewMissingError` at 23:44:21 UTC", but the row in the log it cites reads `2026-10-21T23:44:21.195102+00:00`, and the sibling §78 states "Times are UTC", so the date is a day late — the local CEST date written beside a UTC time.
